questions.scenario: A policy should allow reads only from objects under receipts/ in one S3 bucket. Which resource is correctly scoped?

options.text: arn:aws:s3:::devpolaris-receipts-prod/receipts/*
arn:aws:s3:::devpolaris-receipts-prod
arn:aws:s3:*:*:bucket/devpolaris-receipts-prod
devpolaris-receipts-prod:receipts

questions.explanation: S3 object ARNs include the bucket and object key. The prefix wildcard belongs after receipts/. Learn more in [IAM ARN reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference-arns.html).

questions.scenario: Two security groups share the display name web in different VPCs. An incident command must inspect exactly one of them. Which identifier should the runbook record?

options.text: The Name tag only.
The security group ID and Region.
The console page title.
The creation timestamp only.

questions.explanation: Service resource IDs plus regional context identify the exact resource when friendly names collide. Learn more in [IAM ARN reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference-arns.html).

questions.scenario: A cost anomaly affects resources tagged Environment=prod but half have no Owner tag. What should the platform team fix first?

options.text: Use a longer resource name instead of tags.
Move every resource into one VPC.
Add an enforced ownership tagging standard and remediate missing tags.
Put owner names in IAM policy Sids.

questions.explanation: Consistent ownership and cost-allocation tags make inventory and spend actionable. Learn more in [Tagging AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/tag-editor/latest/userguide/tagging.html).

questions.scenario: A bucket is tagged Confidential=true. A developer assumes the tag alone blocks public access. Which response is correct?

options.text: The tag is an access control by itself.
The tag encrypts objects automatically.
The tag creates an SCP automatically.
The tag is metadata unless a policy or service control explicitly evaluates it.

questions.explanation: Tags are metadata. They influence access only when an IAM, resource, or organization policy uses tag condition keys. Learn more in [Tagging AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/tag-editor/latest/userguide/tagging.html).

questions.scenario: An alert contains an EC2 instance ID and Region. Which evidence should an incident workflow collect before changing it?

options.text: Current tags and owning account.
A guessed resource name based on the application.
Attached security groups, subnet, and IAM role.
Replace stable service identifiers with copied console URLs.
Related CloudTrail events and deployment records.

questions.explanation: Identity, ownership, network placement, runtime role, and change evidence establish what the resource is and why it changed. Learn more in [Tagging AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/tag-editor/latest/userguide/tagging.html).
